title: Appeal 45/3/174: platform stair lift on an upper floor of a converted building; relaxation of Requirement B1 refused
jurisdiction: England (UK): Secretary of State determination / appeal / tribunal under the Building Act 1984 and Building Regulations; comparative test only, not Alberta
code_edition: Building Regulations 2000 (as amended): Requirement B1 (means of warning and escape)

facts.text: The proposed work is a platform stair lift on the second floor of a polytechnic; the building opened in 1951 as a club and was later used as hotel-type accommodation.
A new passenger lift serving the lower levels of the second and third floors was installed, and the existing goods lift serving the upper levels was converted.

The City Council concluded that the stair lift does not comply with Requirement B1 and that relaxation or dispensation would not be appropriate; the appeal papers discuss whether these could be relocated to the lower level.
Determination: relaxation or dispensation with the requirement is neither necessary nor appropriate, and the appeal is dismissed.
